name: Kuwait Petroleum Corporation
desc: Kuwait's national oil company, covering oil and gas production, refining, petrochemicals, shipping and Q8 fuel retail in Europe.
markets: Crude and product exports mainly to Asia; Q8 fuel stations and lubricants in several European countries, including Italy and Belgium.
rationale: Q8 consumer fuel and lubricant brand in Europe plus Gulf B2B hospitality; rival oil majors already sponsor F1.

name: Ecopetrol
desc: Colombia's largest oil and gas company, producing, refining and transporting hydrocarbons and owning power transmission group ISA.
markets: Mainly Colombia; upstream interests in the US Permian Basin and Brazil; ISA transmission networks across Latin America.
rationale: Well-known national brand with Latin American reach; plausible for a Latin America-focused programme, but limited consumer fuel retail abroad.

name: Neste
desc: Finnish refiner and leading producer of renewable diesel and sustainable aviation fuel made from waste and residue oils.
markets: Renewable fuel refineries in Finland, the Netherlands and Singapore; customers across Europe, North America and Asia; fuel stations in Finland.
rationale: Renewable fuel technology fits F1's 2026 move to sustainable fuels; showcase for SAF and renewable diesel with B2B hospitality.

name: Orlen
desc: Polish multi-energy group running refineries, petrochemicals, oil and gas production, power generation and about 3,000 fuel stations.
industry: integrated oil, gas and fuel retail
markets: Fuel retail in Poland, Germany, Czechia, Slovakia, Hungary and Lithuania; upstream assets in Norway; mainly Central Europe.
rationale: Strong consumer fuel brand and past F1 title sponsor with Alfa Romeo; European consumer reach and motorsport heritage.
changed: Merged with Lotos and PGNiG in 2022; renamed from PKN Orlen

name: YPF
desc: Majority state-owned Argentine energy company producing oil and gas, notably Vaca Muerta shale, refining fuels and running service stations.
markets: Customers mainly in Argentina through YPF service stations; growing oil and LNG export ambitions from Vaca Muerta.
rationale: Very visible Argentine consumer fuel brand with motorsport ties; Argentine fan interest in F1 has grown with Franco Colapinto.
changed: Renationalised in 2012

name: OMV
desc: Austrian integrated oil, gas and chemicals group with refineries, gas production, petrochemicals and filling stations in Central Europe.
markets: Fuel retail in Austria and Central and Eastern Europe; upstream in Norway, Romania and other countries; chemicals worldwide via Borealis.
rationale: Consumer fuel brand in Central Europe and chemicals business; rivals sponsor F1; Austrian Grand Prix hospitality is a natural fit.
changed: Agreed with ADNOC in 2025 to combine Borealis and Borouge into Borouge Group International

name: MOL Group
desc: Hungarian oil and gas group running refineries, petrochemicals, upstream assets and about 2,000 filling stations in Central Europe.
industry: integrated oil, gas and fuel retail
markets: Fuel retail in Hungary, Slovakia, Croatia, Romania and other Central European countries; upstream assets including Azerbaijan and Kurdistan.
rationale: Strong consumer fuel brand in Central Europe; Hungarian Grand Prix gives a clear hospitality and activation platform.

name: Pemex
desc: Mexico's state-owned oil company, exploring, producing and refining oil and gas and supplying the Pemex fuel station network.
markets: Fuel sales mainly in Mexico through franchised stations; crude exports and a refinery in Texas (Deer Park).
rationale: Consumer fuel brand in Mexico with a history of backing Sergio Perez; Mexico City Grand Prix fit, but heavy debt.

name: Dangote Petroleum Refinery
desc: Large oil refinery and petrochemical complex in the Lekki Free Zone near Lagos, producing petrol, diesel and aviation fuel.
markets: Supplies the Nigerian fuel market and exports refined products, mainly within West Africa; operations in Nigeria only.
rationale: Dangote is a famous African brand, but the refinery is a B2B fuel supplier; plausible only for an Africa-focused programme.
changed: Began producing fuels in 2024

name: Equinor
desc: Norwegian energy company producing oil and natural gas, mainly on the Norwegian shelf, and developing offshore wind and low-carbon projects.
industry: oil, gas and offshore wind producer
markets: Operations in about 36 countries including Norway, the UK, the US, Brazil and Asia; gas supplier to Europe.
rationale: Global energy brand with sustainability messaging and B2B relationships; plausible but mostly B2B with no fuel retail.
changed: Renamed from Statoil in 2018

name: SSE
desc: British energy company developing renewable power, running electricity networks and thermal plants, and supplying energy in Ireland.
markets: Mainly the UK and Ireland, with renewables development in continental Europe and Japan.
rationale: UK brand recognition and renewables story for British Grand Prix hospitality, but mostly a regulated domestic utility.
changed: Sold its household energy retail business to OVO in 2020

name: CK Hutchison Holdings
desc: Hong Kong conglomerate with ports, health and beauty retail, infrastructure and telecommunications businesses in over 50 countries.
markets: Operations across Europe, Asia and other regions, including Watsons and Superdrug stores, Three mobile networks and Hutchison Ports.
rationale: Retail and telecom consumer brands across Europe and Asia offer activation potential; group itself is a B2B holding.
changed: Formed in 2015 by merging Cheung Kong Holdings and Hutchison Whampoa

name: Nextpower
desc: US maker of solar tracker systems and related software that move panels to follow the sun for utility-scale plants.
markets: Utility-scale solar developers and contractors in the US, Europe, the Middle East, India, Australia and Latin America.
rationale: B2B clean-energy hardware with little consumer awareness; F1 fit limited to sustainability and hospitality.
changed: Spun off from Flex in 2023; renamed Nextpower from Nextracker in 2025

name: SOCAR
desc: Azerbaijan's state oil and gas company, producing in the Caspian, refining, trading and running fuel stations abroad.
markets: Azerbaijan plus fuel retail in Georgia, Switzerland, Ukraine and Romania, refining in Turkey and trading worldwide.
rationale: Experienced sports sponsor with consumer fuel stations in several countries; host-city link with the Azerbaijan Grand Prix in Baku.

name: Ampol
desc: Australian fuel supplier and convenience retailer running the Lytton refinery and over 1,800 Ampol service stations, plus Z Energy.
markets: Australia and New Zealand (Z Energy); fuel trading and supply operations in Singapore and the US.
rationale: Strong Australian consumer fuel brand with motorsport history; Australian Grand Prix in Melbourne is a natural platform.
changed: Renamed from Caltex Australia in 2020; acquired Z Energy in 2022

name: EDP (Energias de Portugal)
desc: Portuguese electric utility generating, distributing and selling power and gas, with renewables arm EDP Renovaveis operating worldwide.
markets: Retail customers in Portugal, Spain and Brazil; renewables in Europe, North America, Latin America and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Iberian consumer brand with a global renewables story; plausible for sustainability-themed partnerships and B2B hospitality.

name: Statkraft
desc: Norwegian state-owned company generating hydropower, wind and solar power, running district heating and trading energy in Europe.
markets: Norway, Sweden, Germany, the UK and other European markets plus Latin America and India; customers are grids, industry and traders.
rationale: Large renewable producer but B2B and state-owned with little consumer brand; weak F1 fit beyond sustainability messaging.

name: Metso
desc: Finnish supplier of crushers, mills, pumps and services for mining, aggregates and metal refining customers.
markets: Mining and construction customers worldwide, with operations in about 50 countries across all main regions.
rationale: B2B equipment maker with a low consumer profile; F1 value limited to B2B hospitality with mining customers.
changed: Formed as Metso Outotec in 2020; renamed Metso in 2023

name: Suncor Energy
desc: Canadian integrated energy company producing oil sands crude, refining fuels and running the Petro-Canada retail station network.
markets: Canada and the US; Petro-Canada stations across Canada and a refinery in Colorado.
rationale: Petro-Canada is a leading consumer brand and experienced sponsor; Canadian Grand Prix in Montreal gives a home platform.

name: SkyNRG
desc: Dutch company that sources, supplies and develops production of sustainable aviation fuel for airlines and corporate travel buyers.
markets: Airlines and corporates in Europe and the US; developing production plants in the Netherlands and the US.
rationale: Sustainable fuel credentials match F1's 2026 sustainable-fuel rules and travel-emissions goals; a niche B2B fit.

name: HELLENiQ Energy
desc: Greek energy group refining crude at three refineries, selling fuels through EKO and BP-branded stations and developing renewables.
markets: Greece, Cyprus and Balkan countries such as Bulgaria, Serbia, North Macedonia and Montenegro.
rationale: Consumer fuel brand in Greece, but no Greek Grand Prix and limited reach; modest F1 fit.
changed: Renamed from Hellenic Petroleum in 2022

name: Rubis
desc: French group distributing fuels, LPG and bitumen and operating storage terminals, with solar power through Photosol.
markets: Caribbean, Africa and Europe, including French overseas territories, Kenya, Jamaica and Switzerland.
rationale: Fuel brands in Caribbean and African markets with no F1 race presence; limited fit.

name: SK On
desc: South Korean maker of lithium-ion battery cells and modules for electric vehicles and energy storage systems.
markets: Carmakers in Korea, the US and Europe, with plants in Korea, the US, Hungary and China.
rationale: Battery technology tie-in with hybrid power units and automaker customers, but B2B with little consumer awareness.
changed: Spun off from SK Innovation in 2021

name: ACWA Power
desc: Saudi developer, investor and operator of power generation, desalinated water and green hydrogen plants.
markets: Projects in about 14 countries across the Middle East, Africa, Central Asia and China.
rationale: Saudi champion aligned with Vision 2030; Saudi Arabian Grand Prix and Gulf B2B hospitality give a plausible fit.

name: CATL (Contemporary Amperex Technology)
desc: Chinese maker of lithium-ion batteries for electric vehicles and energy storage systems, the world's largest by market share.
markets: Supplies carmakers and storage customers worldwide, with plants in China, Germany and Hungary and a project in Spain.
rationale: Global battery leader building its brand abroad, with a clear technology tie-in to hybrid power units and automakers.
changed: Listed in Hong Kong in 2025

name: EDF (Electricite de France)
desc: French state-owned electric utility, the world's largest nuclear operator, generating and selling electricity and gas.
markets: Retail customers in France, the UK, Italy and Belgium; generation and projects in Europe, the Americas, Asia and Africa.
rationale: Very high consumer awareness in France and the UK and an experienced sports sponsor; low-carbon power showcase.
changed: Fully nationalised and delisted in 2023

name: Enel
desc: Italian energy company generating, distributing and selling electricity and gas, and one of the largest renewable power operators.
markets: Italy, Spain and Latin America, plus renewables in North America; tens of millions of customers.
rationale: Strong Italian consumer brand with past Formula E and MotoGP links; Italian Grand Prix hospitality is a fit.

name: Iberdrola
desc: Spanish electric utility generating renewable and other power, running grids and supplying electricity in Spain, the UK and Americas.
markets: Spain, the UK (ScottishPower), the US (Avangrid), Brazil (Neoenergia) and Australia.
rationale: Strong consumer brand in Spain and the UK and an active sports sponsor; Spanish Grand Prix activation is plausible.

name: Mercuria Energy Group
desc: Swiss commodity trading house trading crude oil, refined products, gas, power, metals and agricultural goods, and investing in energy assets.
markets: Trading offices and customers worldwide, including Europe, Asia and the Americas.
rationale: B2B trader with low consumer awareness; F1 use limited to hospitality for trading counterparties.

name: Sysco
desc: US foodservice distributor delivering food, kitchen supplies and equipment to restaurants, hospitals, hotels and schools.
markets: Mainly the US and Canada, plus the UK, Ireland, France, Sweden, Mexico and other markets.
rationale: B2B distributor with limited consumer awareness; F1 fit mainly hospitality for restaurant and hotel customers.

name: Trafigura
desc: Commodity trading house trading oil, refined products, metals, minerals, gas and power, and owning terminals and other logistics assets.
markets: Trading hubs in Geneva, Singapore, Houston, Montevideo and Mumbai; customers and assets worldwide.
rationale: Mostly B2B with low consumer awareness; F1 value limited to hospitality for producers and industrial buyers.

name: AES
desc: US power company generating and distributing electricity, including renewables and battery storage, through utilities and plants.
markets: US utilities in Indiana and Ohio plus generation in Chile, Colombia, Mexico, Panama, the Dominican Republic and other markets.
rationale: Mainly B2B and regulated utility business with moderate brand awareness; weak F1 fit beyond Americas hospitality.

name: Cox
desc: Spanish developer of water desalination, solar power and infrastructure projects, providing engineering, construction and concession operation.
markets: Projects in Spain, Latin America, the Middle East and Africa, including former Abengoa engineering activities.
rationale: B2B infrastructure developer with limited brand awareness; F1 relevance limited to client hospitality.
changed: Acquired Abengoa's businesses in 2023

name: EnBW
desc: German energy company generating, trading and distributing electricity and gas, running grids, offshore wind farms and EV charging.
markets: Mainly Germany, with businesses in Switzerland, Czechia and Turkey and offshore wind in the UK.
rationale: Well-known German utility with EV charging network, but largely domestic and publicly owned; modest F1 fit.

name: Enfinity Global
desc: Renewable energy developer and independent power producer building and operating solar and battery storage projects under long-term contracts.
markets: Projects in the US, Europe (notably Italy and Spain) and Japan, selling power to utilities and corporates.
rationale: B2B renewable developer with little public brand awareness and no consumer customers; weak F1 fit.

name: Engie
desc: French energy group generating and selling electricity and gas, running networks and offering energy efficiency and building services.
markets: Europe, Latin America, North America, the Middle East and Asia-Pacific; strongest consumer presence in France and Belgium.
rationale: Strong consumer brand in France and Belgium with energy-transition story; plausible for European Grand Prix hospitality.
changed: Formed by 2008 merger of Gaz de France and Suez; renamed Engie in 2015

name: Masdar
desc: Abu Dhabi state-owned renewable energy company developing and operating solar, wind, storage and green hydrogen projects.
markets: Projects in over 40 countries across the Middle East, Europe, Asia, Africa and the Americas; customers are utilities and governments.
rationale: UAE flagship sustainability brand; Abu Dhabi Grand Prix offers a home platform for clean-energy messaging.
parent: Abu Dhabi government via TAQA, Mubadala and ADNOC

name: Matrix Renewables
desc: Renewable energy platform developing, building and operating solar and battery storage projects that sell power to utilities.
markets: Projects in the US, Spain, Chile, Mexico, Colombia and other markets; customers are utilities and corporate offtakers.
rationale: B2B solar and storage developer with limited brand awareness and no consumer customers; weak F1 fit.

name: NextEra Energy
desc: US energy company owning utility Florida Power & Light and NextEra Energy Resources, a large wind, solar and storage generator.
markets: United States and Canada; Florida households through FPL and utilities and corporates nationwide.
rationale: Strong Florida utility brand; Miami Grand Prix hospitality is plausible, but business is regulated and North American.

name: RWE
desc: German power generator running offshore and onshore wind, solar, battery storage, gas and hydro plants, and trading energy.
markets: Europe, the United States and Asia-Pacific; customers are utilities and industry.
rationale: Well-known German brand in renewables, but B2B with no consumer retail; modest F1 fit.

name: AESC
desc: Lithium-ion battery maker producing cells and packs for electric vehicles and energy storage at plants in several countries.
markets: Plants in Japan, the UK, France, the US and China; customers are carmakers such as Nissan and Renault.
rationale: B2B battery supplier with limited consumer awareness; technology tie-in exists but F1 fit is modest.
changed: Acquired from Nissan by Envision Group in 2018

name: Darling Ingredients
desc: Converts animal by-products and food waste into fats, proteins, collagen, pet food ingredients and renewable diesel feedstocks.
markets: Over 260 plants on five continents; food, feed, pharma, pet food and fuel customers worldwide.
rationale: B2B ingredients processor with little consumer awareness; renewable diesel link is indirect; weak F1 fit.

name: Octopus Energy Group
desc: British energy supplier selling electricity and gas to households, with smart tariffs, heat pumps, EV charging and renewable generation.
markets: UK retail leader with supply operations in Europe, the US, Japan, Australia and New Zealand.
rationale: Fast-growing consumer brand expanding internationally; EV and smart energy story suits F1 audiences in several markets.
changed: Began separating its Kraken software business in 2025

name: Valero Energy
desc: Large independent petroleum refiner making gasoline, diesel and jet fuel, plus renewable diesel and ethanol, sold wholesale and branded.
markets: United States, Canada, the UK, Ireland, Mexico and Peru; branded stations under Valero, Texaco (UK and Ireland) and others.
rationale: Recognised fuel brand with motorsport history; US races and rivals' F1 sponsorship make it a plausible prospect.

name: LG Energy Solution
desc: South Korean maker of lithium-ion batteries for electric vehicles, energy storage systems and IT devices.
markets: Carmakers and storage customers worldwide, with plants in Korea, the US, Poland, China and Indonesia.
rationale: Global battery supplier with LG brand recognition and a clear technology tie-in to hybrid power units.
changed: Spun off from LG Chem in 2020; listed in 2022

name: AMEA Power
desc: Dubai-based developer, owner and operator of solar, wind and battery storage projects selling power under long-term contracts.
markets: Projects in the Middle East, Africa and Asia, including Egypt, Morocco, Jordan and South Africa.
rationale: B2B developer with no consumer awareness; Gulf hospitality possible but F1 fit is weak.

name: Brookfield Renewable Partners
desc: Owns and operates hydro, wind, solar and storage assets, selling power to utilities and corporates under long-term contracts.
markets: Assets across North America, South America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: B2B infrastructure investor with low consumer awareness; F1 fit limited to hospitality for corporate power buyers.

name: GE Vernova
desc: Makes gas, nuclear, hydro and wind turbines and grid equipment, and services power plants for utilities and industry.
markets: Utilities, governments and industrial buyers worldwide, with operations in over 100 countries.
rationale: Global B2B technology brand with GE heritage; engineering showcase and hospitality give a plausible F1 fit.
changed: Spun off from General Electric in 2024

name: Raizen
desc: Brazilian joint venture producing sugar and ethanol from cane and distributing fuels at Shell-branded service stations.
markets: Mainly Brazil; sugar and ethanol exported to international buyers.
rationale: Strong Brazilian consumer exposure via Shell stations; Sao Paulo Grand Prix fit, but financially stretched.
f1: Shell (Ferrari partner) co-controls Raizen and licenses it the Shell fuel brand in Brazil

name: SLB
desc: Oilfield services and technology company providing reservoir, drilling, well completion, production and digital services to energy producers.
markets: Customers in more than 100 countries across all main regions.
rationale: Global B2B technology brand with no consumer awareness; data and engineering showcase gives a plausible F1 angle.
changed: Renamed from Schlumberger in 2022; acquired ChampionX in 2025

name: Zelestra
desc: Spanish renewable energy developer building and operating solar, wind and storage projects that sell power to utilities and corporates.
markets: Projects in Spain, Italy, other European countries, the US and Latin America.
rationale: Private equity-owned B2B renewable developer with no consumer visibility or brand-marketing need; weak F1 fit.
changed: Acquired as Solarpack by EQT in 2021; renamed Zelestra in 2024

name: Orsted
desc: Danish renewable energy company developing, building and operating offshore wind farms, plus onshore wind, solar and storage.
markets: Europe, North America and Asia-Pacific; customers are utilities, corporates and governments.
rationale: Mostly B2B and focused on restructuring after US project setbacks; recognised in Denmark and the UK; modest F1 fit.
changed: Renamed from DONG Energy in 2017

name: GreenYellow
desc: French company designing, financing and operating solar power plants and energy efficiency services for commercial and industrial clients.
markets: Commercial and industrial clients in France, Brazil, Colombia, South-East Asia and Africa.
rationale: B2B solar and energy efficiency provider with limited public awareness; weak F1 fit.
changed: Acquired from Casino Group by Ardian (deal agreed in 2022)

name: nVent
desc: Makes electrical enclosures, connection and fastening products and liquid cooling systems for data centres and industry.
markets: Industrial, utility, infrastructure and data centre customers in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: B2B component brand with low consumer awareness; data centre cooling gives a small technology angle.
changed: Spun off from Pentair in 2018; sold thermal management business in 2025

name: Poste Italiane
desc: Italy's postal, parcel and financial services group offering payments, savings, insurance, mobile and energy services.
markets: Customers in Italy only; about 12,800 post offices nationwide.
rationale: Household name in Italy and an active sports sponsor; Italian Grand Prix activation is plausible, but domestic only.
parent: Italian state (Ministry of Economy and CDP)

name: Technip Energies
desc: Engineering and technology company designing and building LNG, hydrogen, ethylene and carbon capture plants for energy producers.
markets: Energy and chemicals clients in Europe, the Middle East, Asia-Pacific and the Americas.
rationale: B2B engineering firm with no consumer awareness; weak F1 fit beyond hospitality.
changed: Spun off from TechnipFMC in 2021

name: Westinghouse Electric Company
desc: Designs nuclear reactors, including the AP1000, supplies nuclear fuel and provides services and maintenance to nuclear plants.
markets: Utilities and governments in North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: B2B nuclear supplier with sector profile but no consumer brand; weak F1 fit.
changed: Emerged from bankruptcy in 2018; acquired by Brookfield and Cameco in 2023

name: Baker Hughes
desc: Energy technology company providing oilfield services and equipment, turbines, compressors and LNG technology to energy and industrial customers.
markets: Customers in over 120 countries; co-headquartered in Houston and London.
rationale: Global B2B technology brand; engineering showcase and client hospitality give a plausible F1 fit.
changed: Formed in 2017 by combining Baker Hughes with GE Oil & Gas

name: Carrier Global
desc: Makes heating, ventilation, air conditioning and refrigeration systems for homes and buildings under Carrier, Viessmann and other brands.
markets: Homeowners, buildings and contractors in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Widely known brand with international reach; climate technology and B2B hospitality give a plausible fit.
changed: Spun off from United Technologies in 2020; acquired Viessmann Climate Solutions in 2024

name: Sinopec Group
desc: Chinese state-owned oil and petrochemical group whose listed arm Sinopec Corp refines fuel and runs about 30,000 stations.
markets: Fuel retail mainly in China; upstream, trading and engineering operations in many countries.
rationale: Strong Chinese consumer fuel brand; Chinese Grand Prix and lubricants offer a fit, but state ownership may limit appetite.

name: Sunwoda Electronic
desc: Chinese lithium-ion battery maker producing battery packs for phones and laptops, electric vehicle batteries and energy storage systems.
markets: Consumer electronics brands and carmakers in China and worldwide, with factories in China and overseas.
rationale: B2B supplier with low consumer recognition outside Asia; battery technology angle but weak brand-marketing culture.

name: TotalEnergies
desc: French integrated energy company producing oil and gas, refining, selling fuel at service stations and growing in LNG and renewables.
markets: Operations in more than 120 countries, with fuel retail across Europe and Africa.
rationale: Very recognisable consumer brand with long motorsport history, including past F1 partnerships; rivals sponsor F1 today.
changed: Renamed from Total in 2021

name: Clarios
desc: Makes low-voltage automotive batteries, including 12-volt and start-stop batteries, for carmakers and the aftermarket under Varta and Optima.
markets: Carmakers and aftermarket customers in North America, Europe, Asia and Latin America, with dozens of plants worldwide.
rationale: Varta and Optima are aftermarket consumer brands; automotive supplier link makes F1 plausible for B2B hospitality.
changed: Carved out of Johnson Controls by a Brookfield-led group in 2019

name: Contemporary Amperex Intel..
desc: Ningde-based company whose name indicates a CATL group affiliate; Crunchbase lists battery and automotive activities, details unconfirmed.
markets: Operations in China; customers and international activity not confirmed.
rationale: Exact business unconfirmed; any F1 interest would run through CATL itself rather than this unit.

name: First Solar
desc: US maker of thin-film cadmium telluride solar modules sold to utility-scale solar developers and power producers.
markets: Mainly the US and India, with factories in the US, India, Malaysia and Vietnam.
rationale: B2B manufacturer with modest brand awareness; US-made clean technology story, but weak F1 fit.

name: Qcells
desc: US arm of Hanwha's solar business, making solar modules in Georgia and selling modules, storage and residential solar.
markets: US installers, utilities and homeowners; parent Qcells sells worldwide from Korea and Germany.
rationale: Strong solar brand with sports sponsorship history; US-focused unit makes F1 fit only plausible via Hanwha.

name: APR Energy
desc: Provides fast-track mobile gas turbine power plants that supply temporary electricity to utilities, governments and industry.
markets: Utilities, governments and industrial customers in the Americas, the Middle East, Africa and Asia.
rationale: B2B power rental business with no consumer profile or marketing culture; weak F1 fit.
changed: Acquired by Atlas Corp in 2020

name: Avnet
desc: US distributor of electronic components and embedded solutions supplying equipment manufacturers worldwide.
markets: Manufacturers and OEMs across the Americas, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Direct rival Arrow Electronics sponsors F1; engineering B2B audience and hospitality make a plausible fit.

name: Repsol
desc: Spanish energy company producing oil and gas, refining, making chemicals and renewable power, and running about 4,500 service stations.
markets: Fuel retail in Spain, Portugal, Mexico and Peru; upstream in the Americas, Europe, Africa and Asia.
rationale: Long-standing motorsport sponsor with high consumer visibility; rivals sponsor F1 and Spanish Grand Prix offers activation.

name: Gotion High-tech
desc: Chinese maker of lithium iron phosphate batteries for electric vehicles and energy storage systems.
markets: Carmakers and storage buyers in China and abroad, with plants in China, Germany and other countries.
rationale: B2B battery supplier with little consumer awareness; Volkswagen link offers some automotive angle, but weak fit.
changed: Volkswagen Group became largest shareholder in 2020

name: SQM (Sociedad Quimica y Minera)
desc: Chilean producer of lithium, iodine, potassium nitrate and specialty plant nutrients from the Atacama salt flats.
markets: Battery makers, farms and industrial firms worldwide; lithium operations in Chile and Australia.
rationale: B2B commodity producer with little consumer brand; EV battery link is indirect; weak F1 fit.
changed: Formed lithium joint venture with Codelco in 2025

name: Trina Solar
desc: Chinese manufacturer of solar modules, trackers and energy storage products for utilities, developers and installers.
markets: Customers worldwide, with sales across Asia, Europe, the Americas and the Middle East.
rationale: Industry brand that sponsors events; plausible B2B and sustainability fit but limited consumer awareness.

name: Power Corporation of Canada
desc: Canadian holding company controlling insurer Great-West Lifeco and wealth manager IGM Financial, plus alternative asset investments.
markets: Canada, the US and Europe through Canada Life, Empower, Irish Life and IGM.
rationale: Holding company without its own consumer brand; subsidiaries are mostly North American; weak F1 fit.

name: Shanghai Electric Group
desc: Chinese state-controlled maker of thermal, wind, nuclear and grid power equipment, also providing industrial services.
markets: Mainly China, with power projects in Asia, the Middle East and Africa.
rationale: State-controlled B2B equipment manufacturer with little consumer awareness outside China; weak F1 fit.

name: Sensata Technologies
desc: Designs and makes sensors, switches, controls and electrical protection components for vehicles, aircraft and industrial equipment.
markets: Automotive, truck, aerospace and industrial customers in the Americas, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Automotive sensor supplier with a technology tie-in; B2B with little consumer awareness.

name: Hitachi Energy
desc: Makes transformers, high-voltage direct current systems, grid automation and software for utilities, industry and renewable developers.
markets: Utilities and industry worldwide, with operations in about 60 countries.
rationale: B2B electrification brand with sponsorship track record; grid and electrification tech showcase is plausible.
changed: Hitachi acquired ABB Power Grids in 2020 (full ownership 2022); renamed Hitachi Energy in 2021

name: World Kinect Corporation
desc: Supplies and trades aviation, marine and land fuels, and sells power, natural gas and sustainability services.
markets: Airlines, shipping lines, governments and commercial fleets in about 200 countries.
rationale: B2B fuel logistics brand known in aviation and shipping; sustainable fuels and hospitality give a modest fit.
changed: Renamed from World Fuel Services in 2023

name: LG Innotek
desc: South Korean maker of smartphone camera modules, automotive electronics, semiconductor substrates and other electronic components.
markets: Smartphone makers, carmakers and chip companies worldwide; most revenue from camera modules for iPhone.
rationale: B2B component brand unknown to consumers; automotive electronics gives a slight angle; weak F1 fit.

name: Anker Innovations
desc: Chinese consumer electronics company selling Anker chargers and power banks, Soundcore audio, eufy smart home and Nebula projectors.
markets: Sold through Amazon, retailers and its own sites in over 100 countries, strongest in North America, Europe and Japan.
rationale: Brand-led global consumer electronics company with sports marketing; charging and power products suit F1 audiences.

name: JinkoSolar
desc: Chinese solar module manufacturer, vertically integrated from wafers to modules, selling panels to utilities, developers and installers.
markets: Customers in over 100 countries, with factories in China, South-East Asia and the US.
rationale: Large B2B solar brand that has used sports sponsorship; plausible sustainability fit with limited consumer awareness.

name: Alcoa
desc: US aluminium producer mining bauxite, refining alumina and smelting aluminium for automotive, packaging and construction manufacturers.
markets: Operations in Australia, Brazil, Canada, Spain, Norway, Iceland and the US; customers worldwide.
rationale: B2B commodity supplier with little consumer awareness; lightweight materials story gives only a modest F1 angle.
changed: Acquired Alumina Limited in 2024

name: Newmont
desc: Largest gold mining company, producing gold with copper, silver and zinc from mines in several countries.
markets: Mines in the US, Canada, Mexico, Ghana, Australia, Peru, Argentina, Papua New Guinea and Suriname.
rationale: B2B gold producer with little consumer visibility; F1 use limited to investor and partner hospitality; weak fit.
changed: Acquired Newcrest Mining in 2023

name: Nippon Steel Corporation
desc: Japan's largest steelmaker, producing steel for automotive, construction and energy customers, and owner of U.S. Steel.
markets: Japan, the US, India and South-East Asia, with customers worldwide.
rationale: B2B steelmaker with little consumer profile; Japanese Grand Prix hospitality is possible but fit is weak.
changed: Acquired U.S. Steel in 2025

name: Vale
desc: Brazilian miner and one of the largest producers of iron ore and pellets, also producing nickel and copper.
industry: iron ore and base metals mining
markets: Steelmakers mainly in China, Asia and Europe; operations in Brazil, Canada and Indonesia.
rationale: Strong Brazilian brand recognition with sponsorship history; Sao Paulo Grand Prix fit, but B2B commodity producer.
changed: Privatised in 1997; rebranded from Companhia Vale do Rio Doce to Vale in 2007

name: Vedanta Resources
desc: Holding company of Indian resources group Vedanta, producing zinc, aluminium, copper, iron ore, oil, gas and power.
markets: Mainly India, with mining assets in Zambia, South Africa and Namibia.
rationale: Indian commodities group with modest consumer awareness and high debt; weak F1 fit.
changed: Delisted from the London Stock Exchange in 2018

name: Zijin Mining
desc: Chinese miner producing gold, copper, zinc, lithium and silver from mines in China and abroad.
markets: Operations in China and over a dozen countries across Asia, Africa, Europe, the Americas and Oceania.
rationale: B2B commodity producer with limited brand awareness outside China; weak F1 fit.

name: Barrick Mining
desc: Canadian gold and copper miner operating large mines in North America, Africa, Latin America and Asia.
markets: Mines and projects in about 18 countries, including the US, Canada, Argentina, the Democratic Republic of Congo and Pakistan.
rationale: Global resources brand with limited consumer awareness; F1 use limited to investor hospitality; weak fit.
